title: Welcome
open: Start Penguin cpp with no document open.
purpose: Start a new session, reopen recent files, or reach the main preferences.
controls: Open an existing source file or project.
result: Open a document to switch to the editor.

title: Main window
open: Open a source file or project.
purpose: Write code, navigate a project, build it, and inspect compiler messages.
controls: Choose the build configuration and compilation actions.
Switch the left panel between files, symbols and debugger watches.
Switch files, fold code and manage breakpoints.
Read errors, build output, debugger output and search results.
result: Double-click a compiler error to move to its source line.
note: On macOS, File, Edit, Search and the other menus are in the system menu bar above the window.

title: New Project
purpose: Create a project from a template.
controls: Choose a starting structure suited to the target.
Name the project before saving its .dev file.
Choose the source language when the template offers a choice.
result: Save the project in its own folder. Templates do not install external SDKs.

title: Project Options
purpose: Configure the current project rather than the whole IDE.
controls: Per-file compile/link choices and build priority.
Compiler options and additional compiler or linker arguments.
Include and library folders, custom builds and output locations.
result: OK applies the working copy. Cancel discards this dialog’s changes.
note: Project metadata inherited from Windows does not make a native macOS/Linux build support every Windows resource.

title: Editor Options
purpose: Control editing behaviour and code presentation.
controls: Indentation, tabs, navigation and editing behaviour.
Code font, line-number gutter and syntax colours.
Reusable code, completion and symbol insertion.
Configure automatic saving; keep backups for important work.
result: OK applies the settings. Cancel leaves your saved preferences unchanged.

title: Fonts and line numbers
purpose: Choose a readable monospaced font and the number gutter.
controls: Choose an installed family and a size between 6 and 72 points.
Show the margin and its line labels.
Fit the digit count automatically or choose a minimum digit count.
result: The line numbers follow the editor font and zoom.
note: A separate gutter font is disabled in the native editor. The legacy ligatures switch is not wired to rendering in 0.5.6; do not rely on it.

title: Environment Options
purpose: Set general IDE behaviour, terminal preferences and interface choices.
controls: Console pause, backups and window behaviour.
Change the UI text rather than the code font.
Choose Automatic or an installed terminal for console programs.
Inspect the available environment categories before applying changes.
result: Use Editor Options for the font inside source files.

title: Compiler Options
purpose: Manage compiler configurations and their tools.
controls: Select a Release, Debug or Profiling configuration.
Choose language, warnings, optimisation and debugging options.
Set executable, include and library search paths.
Check the compiler, make and debugger executable names.
result: Select the intended configuration in the main toolbar before building.
note: A library also needs matching headers, binaries, architecture and linker flags; adding an include path alone is not enough.

title: Find and replace
open: Search → Find / Replace / Find in Files
purpose: Locate text or replace occurrences with a controlled scope.
controls: Choose finding, replacing, or searching multiple files.
Enter the search text and, for replacement, the new text.
Match case or whole words when needed.
Limit the operation to a selection, the current file, open files or a project.
result: Review multi-file matches before replacing broadly. Save or back up important files.

title: Go to line
purpose: Jump directly to a line number.
controls: Enter the line reported by the compiler or another person.
Move the caret to that line.
result: The document stays unchanged.

title: File properties
purpose: Inspect the selected source file.
controls: Choose a file when more than one is available.
Check which file you are inspecting.
Review line and character counts shown by the dialog.
result: Use this to confirm a file’s identity before investigating a build problem.

title: Program parameters
purpose: Supply arguments to a program or a host executable for a library project.
controls: Arguments passed to the launched program.
An executable that loads a dynamic library, when applicable.
result: Arguments are not compiler flags or text typed into standard input.
note: A normal console program usually needs no host application.

title: CPU Window
open: While debugging is paused, use the CPU window button in the Debug panel.
purpose: Inspect low-level debugger information.
controls: Machine instructions near the paused location.
Register names and values reported by the debugger.
Frames leading to the current stop.
Choose the assembly syntax supported by the backend.
result: Pause at a breakpoint before expecting live data.
note: This capture shows an idle view. Windows-target debugging remains a separate limitation of the compatibility environment.

title: Profile Analysis
purpose: Inspect measurements collected from an instrumented native program.
controls: Sort and compare functions reported by the profiler.
Hide unused or static functions and change the minimum call count.
Recompute the displayed result with the selected filters.
result: Use the Profiling configuration, rebuild and execute the program first.
note: On macOS the LLVM view counts calls; it does not measure time or show the gprof call graph. The screenshot contains real output from the tutorial program.

title: Tools Configuration
purpose: Keep shortcuts to external programs.
controls: Change their order in the menu.
result: A tool entry does not install the program it names.

title: Edit Tool Entry
open: Tools → Configure Tools → Add or Edit
purpose: Describe how an external program should be launched.
controls: Label shown in the Tools menu.
Executable and folder in which to run it.
result: Check paths and arguments before launching a tool that modifies files.

title: Window List
purpose: Switch among open editor documents.
controls: Use the displayed name and location to distinguish files.
result: This does not browse unopened files on disk.

title: Add TODO item
open: Use the editor’s TODO insertion action.
purpose: Record a development task in the source.
result: Confirming inserts a comment; it does not create a GitHub issue.

title: TODO List
purpose: Find task comments in the selected scope.
controls: Choose which task comments to list.
Update the list and jump to a task’s source.
result: The sample program includes a TODO comment so the list has a real source to inspect.

title: New Template From Project
open: File → New → Template, with a project open.
purpose: Reuse a project structure for later projects.
controls: Choose which project files to include.
Save the template once the required fields are filled.
result: Templates reuse a structure; they do not bundle every external dependency.
note: The separate icon-library dialog has a legacy resource-loading problem in 0.5.6. Do not depend on that auxiliary picker.

title: New Class
open: Classes pane → context menu → class creation action
purpose: Prepare a C++ class declaration through the class-browser tools.
controls: Describe the new class and optional parent.
Use the available selection controls for the current project.
result: Inspect the generated code and its destination before saving.
note: Availability depends on the current project and class-browser selection. This is not a general refactoring engine.

title: New Function
open: Classes pane → context menu → function creation action
purpose: Prepare a function or class member.
controls: Select a target class and access level where available.
result: Review the declaration and implementation after insertion.

title: New Variable
open: Classes pane → context menu → variable creation action
purpose: Prepare a variable or class member.
controls: Request accessors where the tool offers them.
result: Review the generated names and code before saving.

title: Go to Function
purpose: Navigate functions parsed from the current code.
controls: Move the editor to the selected function.
result: Save valid code and let the parser update if a symbol is missing.

title: Remove from project
purpose: Remove selected units from the current project.
controls: Select the project entries to remove.
result: Check the selected project entries before confirming.
note: Keep a backup of files you want to preserve; do not use project removal as a substitute for checking the files on disk.

title: Print File
purpose: Choose source-code print or PDF settings.
controls: Choose the presentation of the output.
Include or omit source line labels.
Continue to the available PDF or printer workflow.
result: Inspect the resulting PDF or print preview before sharing it.
note: Printer setup depends on the OS and installed printers; the screenshot shows this Mac’s available choices.

title: Incremental Search
purpose: Search while entering a query in a small floating bar.
controls: Type to move among matching text.
Use the available navigation keys; close the bar when finished.
result: Use the full Find dialog when you need replacement or a multi-file scope.

title: Tip Of The Day
purpose: Read short usage hints.
controls: Choose whether to show this dialog automatically.
result: Some tips describe inherited editor behaviour; use this manual for the current platform limits.

title: Artistic Style options
purpose: Choose how astyle formats code.
controls: Choose a brace and indentation style.
Adjust spacing, indentation and other formatting rules.
Compare the sample before applying the style.
result: Use Formatting → Format Current File to format the active source. Undo is available for editor formatting.

title: ClangFormat options
purpose: Configure the optional clang-format formatter.
controls: Start from a supported formatting style.
Override indentation, braces, spacing and line-length choices.
Available when the formatter executable can be found.
result: Install or configure clang-format before expecting a live preview.
note: clang-format was not installed in this capture environment. The default bundled macOS formatter is astyle; do not run apt commands on macOS.

title: Attach to process
purpose: Choose an already-running process for a native debugger session.
controls: Select the intended process; verify its name and PID.
Ask the configured debugger to attach.
result: Use a process you own and compiled with debug information.
note: macOS permissions and signing can prevent attachment. This does not enable debugging arbitrary Windows programs through Wine.

title: First-time configuration
open: The initial configuration wizard; also use welcome actions for later changes.
purpose: Choose an interface language, appearance and code font.
controls: Choose the available appearance and syntax scheme.
Pick an installed monospaced family for code.
result: The manual and screenshots use English. Your browser can translate the manual text.

title: About Penguin cpp
open: Help → About Penguin cpp; on macOS also check the application menu.
purpose: Check the installed version and project credits.
controls: Identify which build you are using.
Read the project’s author and development credits.
Open the project, version notes and licence documentation.
result: Include the version when reporting a problem.

title: Windows compatibility
purpose: Choose when to compile and run Windows-target programs.
controls: Let includes guide the target or choose one explicitly.
Compile and execute the environment’s self-test when tools are available.
Choose Unicode UTF-8, OEM 437, ANSI 1252 or program-controlled output.
Use custom toolchain, runtime and prefix paths only when needed.
result: Save the selection, then use Compile & Run. Rebuild after changing the console profile.
note: The complete macOS PKG/DMG includes LLVM-MinGW, Make and Wine ARM64/FEX. Compatibility is experimental; graphics.h/WinBGIm and Windows debugging are not fully covered.

title: Preparing Windows compatibility
open: The complete environment starts its first-use check automatically.
purpose: Prepare a private Windows environment and check the included compiler and runtime before building your program.
controls: Show the current check. Prefix creation may take a while on first use.
Stop preparation if you need to return to the editor.
result: Wait for Environment ready. If preparation fails, read its details, correct the cause and retry.
note: This capture uses the actual included tools and a disposable environment. The setup does not download Apple GPTK or accept its licence.

title: Environment ready
open: Shown after the first-use environment check succeeds.
purpose: Confirm that the included compiler built the test program and the runtime executed it successfully.
controls: The preparation window closes automatically after this confirmation.
result: Use Compile & Run for a Windows-target program. Your program uses this prepared private environment.
note: A successful smoke test does not guarantee support for every Windows API, graphics library or external SDK.

title: Check for updates
purpose: Compare the installed version with the latest published GitHub release.
controls: Read whether an update is available or the connection failed.
Install through the supported platform flow or open the release download.
Check again after a connection problem.
Read changes and known limits before updating.
result: On Linux the update flow uses APT; on macOS the full channel keeps the complete environment.
note: The screenshot shows a real check from 0.5.6. Update controls may be disabled when there is no newer version.
